Summary: AG Sprint 3 — Human Approval, Real Agent/MCP, and AI Explanations
Description: Deliver a governed end-to-end workflow in which real agent tool requests are allowed, denied, or held for human approval and fully audited.

Summary: Complete the human approval lifecycle
Description: Provide a secure approval queue and deterministic state transitions for sensitive agent actions.
Acceptance Criteria: Authorized approvers can approve or reject pending requests, self-approval and invalid transitions are blocked, and every transition is audited.

Summary: Implement approval queue and detail APIs
Description: Add organization-scoped list, filter, and detail endpoints for pending and completed approvals.

Summary: Implement approve, reject, expire, and cancel transitions
Description: Enforce valid state transitions and persist reviewer, reason, timestamps, and final outcome.

Summary: Prevent self-approval and duplicate processing
Description: Block requesters from approving their own actions and make approval operations idempotent.

Summary: Execute governed tools safely
Description: Create a tool-execution layer that runs an external action only after AgentGuard authorizes it.
Acceptance Criteria: Denied requests never execute, approval-required requests execute only after approval, and successful or failed executions are recorded exactly once.

Summary: Create provider-neutral tool adapter interface
Description: Define a common adapter contract for tool discovery, argument validation, execution, and normalized results.

Summary: Add idempotent execution records
Description: Store execution status, attempt count, timestamps, provider response, and idempotency key.

Summary: Handle tool timeout, failure, and retry safely
Description: Add bounded timeouts, safe retry rules, failure auditing, and user-visible error states.

Summary: Integrate a real AI agent
Description: Connect one real AI agent that proposes tool calls through the AgentGuard governance gateway.
Acceptance Criteria: The agent can submit structured tool requests, cannot bypass AgentGuard, and its request, decision, and result share one correlation ID.

Summary: Implement agent adapter and structured request schema
Description: Translate agent tool-call proposals into the common AgentGuard action-request model.

Summary: Register agent identity and permitted capabilities
Description: Bind the agent to its registered identity, owner, permitted tools, and environment.

Summary: Add mock mode for deterministic local and CI testing
Description: Provide a provider-free mock agent so tests and demonstrations do not depend on external availability.

Summary: Integrate one MCP tool provider
Description: Connect AgentGuard to one MCP server, such as a safely configured Zapier MCP endpoint, using a small allowlisted tool set.
Acceptance Criteria: AgentGuard discovers only approved tools, validates arguments, governs each invocation, and successfully demonstrates at least two non-destructive test actions.

Summary: Configure MCP client and secret handling
Description: Load the MCP endpoint and credentials from environment variables and document secure setup.

Summary: Allowlist safe MCP tools and argument schemas
Description: Expose only selected non-destructive tools and validate destination, channel, sheet, or project constraints.

Summary: Implement MCP mock server or stub
Description: Provide deterministic local and CI behavior when the real MCP service is unavailable.

Summary: Explain policy decisions with AI without changing them
Description: Generate grounded plain-language explanations from the immutable deterministic decision record.
Acceptance Criteria: Explanations reference the matched policy and request context, follow a validated schema, and can never alter the authorization decision.

Summary: Create model-provider abstraction and mock provider
Description: Support a configurable AI provider and a deterministic local fallback.

Summary: Build grounded explanation prompt and output schema
Description: Provide only approved decision data and validate the returned summary, rationale, and caution fields.

Summary: Handle AI provider failure safely
Description: Return the original deterministic decision and a safe fallback explanation when the provider fails.

Summary: Add agent and MCP security guardrails
Description: Protect the governance path from prompt injection, unsafe arguments, secret leakage, and direct tool bypass.
Acceptance Criteria: Malicious prompts and tool arguments are rejected or escalated, secrets are redacted, and tests prove that no execution bypasses policy evaluation.

Summary: Validate and sanitize tool arguments
Description: Reject unexpected fields, unsafe destinations, destructive actions, and oversized payloads.

Summary: Add prompt-injection and bypass test cases
Description: Create an evaluation set covering instruction override, hidden actions, direct execution, and policy-evasion attempts.

Summary: Redact secrets and sensitive fields from logs and prompts
Description: Define redaction rules and verify that credentials and sensitive values are not exposed.

Summary: Provide an end-to-end governance interface
Description: Expose pending approvals, execution status, agent requests, policy decisions, and AI explanations in the React application.
Acceptance Criteria: A reviewer can complete the full request-to-decision-to-approval-to-execution workflow from the web interface.

Summary: Build approval queue and review screens
Description: Add filters, request context, matched policy, approve/reject forms, and reviewer notes.

Summary: Display execution timeline and correlation data
Description: Show request, decision, approval, execution, result, and audit events as one trace.

Summary: Display grounded AI explanations and failure states
Description: Present explanations separately from the authoritative decision and handle provider errors clearly.

Summary: Test, document, and demonstrate Sprint 3
Description: Provide repeatable test evidence, release documentation, Jira evidence, and a sprint review recording for the real governed-agent workflow.
Acceptance Criteria: Backend, frontend, approval, MCP, security, and end-to-end tests pass and the Sprint 3 demonstration shows allow, deny, approval, execution, and audit scenarios.

Summary: Add approval, agent, MCP, and end-to-end tests
Description: Cover state transitions, idempotency, provider failure, bypass prevention, and governed execution.

Summary: Update architecture, threat model, and AI evaluation docs
Description: Document adapters, trust boundaries, failure behavior, model limitations, and security controls.

Summary: Create Sprint 3 release notes and demo evidence
Description: Record completed stories, limitations, test results, screenshots, Jira links, and sprint review video.
